column1: # The frozen corpus. expected <TAB> origin <TAB> prompt
# FROZEN ON PURPOSE. This file is the answer key, and a reading is only comparable
# to another reading taken against the SAME key — which is why `evals/run` prints
# this file's hash beside every verdict. Regenerating it RESETS THE BASELINE: every
# earlier percentage stops being comparable, so do it deliberately, never as a
# side effect of editing a skill.
# The trap this guards: if the cases were derived from each description at run time,
# improving a description would move the skill AND the test together, and the delta
# — the entire product of this instrument — would mean nothing.
#   quoted           the phrase appears IN QUOTES inside the skill's own description.
#                    A failure here is unambiguous: the skill will not fire on its
#   derived          the skill declares this branch in prose but quotes no phrase, so
#                    the wording is a faithful reading of that branch rather than a
#                    copy. A failure here is softer — the wording is one of several
#   control-negative must fire NO harness skill. If one fires, the INSTRUMENT is wrong.
#   control-positive a skill is named outright, so a Skill call is near-certain. It
#                    asks "can this instrument SEE a Skill call?", never "is the
#                    harness good" — keeping instrument health separate from the
#                    reading, so a real harness regression is never mis-reported as
# Only the 12 model-invocable skills appear. The 4 user-invoked ones
# disable-model-invocation, so a model cannot fire them at all and measuring them
# would be asking a question with a known, uninteresting answer.
# The language is each description's own. Where a skill quotes Spanish triggers the
# case is Spanish; where its prose is English the derived case is English. This
# corpus deliberately measures the phrases the harness ALREADY DECLARES, not the way
# a person actually talks — see evals/README.md.
